ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, unspecified

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Dome-shaped, red papules and nodules on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
key_facts: 12-year history of itchy eruptions
Nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously
Gradual increase in number and size of nodules
Otherwise healthy patient
No family history of inherited ichthyosis or atopy
Normal routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests
No atypical cells in the peripheral blood
Clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor on DNA analysis
Atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis on biopsy
Dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis on biopsy
Small to medium-sized, atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism on biopsy
Positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO on immunohistochemical staining

shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, consistent with clinical presentation and histopathology findings

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to mycosis fungoides, with potential for systemic involvement and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, unspecified
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathology findings consistent with a peripheral T-cell lymphoma, although specific subtype cannot be determined
